back: A material made of long chain molecules. Most are synthetic plastics from crude oil; biopolymers are made from plants.
Thermoforming. Glass-like clarity or bright colours, hard, rigid and weather resistant, but scratches and can be brittle — signs, displays, light fittings.
Trade name for extruded polystyrene foam (blue). Very light and easy to cut, carve and sand — block models and prototypes.
Modelling foams such as polyurethane board are denser and harder, hold sharp detail and can be CNC machined — for high-quality models.
Thermoforming. Tough, impact resistant, rigid, injection moulds and 3D prints well — electronic casings, LEGO, helmets.
Thermoforming. Tough, hard-wearing, low friction (self-lubricating) — gears, bearings, cable ties, zips.
Thermosetting. Two-part (resin + hardener), very strong adhesive, hard and chemically resistant — adhesives, carbon-fibre composites, PCBs.
A polymer that softens when heated and can be reshaped many times, because its chains are not bonded to each other.
A polymer that sets permanently when first heated or cured, because cross-links form between its chains.
Can be reshaped and usually recycled, many colours — but soften when hot, often less scratch resistant, some go brittle in UV light.
Keep their shape when hot, hard, excellent insulators, chemically resistant — but cannot be reshaped, hard to recycle, often brittle.

front: Why are polymers used for plugs and cable sheathing?
back: They are electrical insulators, protecting users from electric shock. Thermosets also resist heat.

front: Why are foamed polymers good thermal insulators?
back: They trap air in tiny cells, slowing the flow of heat.
Special polymers that do conduct electricity — used in flexible electronics and touch-sensitive surfaces.
The ability to stretch or bend and return to the original shape — e.g. polypropylene living hinges on bottle lids.
A polymer made from renewable sources such as corn starch, sugar cane or cellulose instead of crude oil — e.g. PLA.
Made from renewable crops, usually a lower carbon footprint, and many are compostable.
Often more brittle and less heat resistant, more expensive, most need industrial composting, crops use farmland, and they can contaminate plastic recycling.
Makes them fade, discolour and become brittle — slowed by UV-resistant coatings and stabilisers.
The shape, colour and texture come straight from the mould, so no further finish is needed.
